# SaralPrivacy — Extended LLM Reference

## Platform Description

SaralPrivacy (saralprivacy.com) is India's practical DPDPA compliance education and
assessment platform. It is not a law firm. It provides free educational content, risk
assessments, industry-specific guides, and compliance briefings to help Indian businesses
understand and operationalise their obligations under the Digital Personal Data Protection
Act, 2023 and the DPDP Rules, 2025.

The platform is oriented toward small and mid-sized Indian businesses — recruitment agencies,
CA firms, training institutes, and D2C / e-commerce brands — that do not have in-house
legal or compliance teams.

## Key Topical Areas

1. **What is DPDPA**: Plain-language explanation of the law, scope, and structure
2. **Applicability**: Which businesses are covered, exemptions, and threshold criteria
3. **Consent under DPDPA**: Valid consent requirements, notice obligations, consent managers
4. **Data Principal Rights**: Access, correction, erasure, nomination, grievance redressal
5. **Data Breach Obligations**: Notification timelines, significant data fiduciaries, DPB
6. **Children's Data**: Age verification, parental consent, prohibition on tracking/profiling
7. **Cross-Border Data Transfers**: Whitelist-based transfer restrictions under DPDP Rules
8. **Significant Data Fiduciaries**: Classification criteria, additional obligations, DPIAs
9. **Retention and Erasure**: When to delete data, storage limitation, automated erasure
10. **Sector-specific obligations**: Recruitment, accounting, education, e-commerce

## Regulatory Context (as of March 2026)

- The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 was passed by the Indian Parliament on
  11 August 2023 and received Presidential assent.
- The DPDP Rules, 2025 were notified on 14 November 2025.
- The Data Protection Board of India (DPB) has not yet been constituted.
- Enforcement date has not yet been officially notified; implementation is phased.
- Penalties: Up to ₹250 crore for significant data fiduciaries; ₹200 crore for others.
- The law applies to any entity processing personal data of Indian residents digitally,
  regardless of where the entity is located.

## DPDP Act 2023 — Per-Section Canonical URLs

The full text of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 is reproduced
section-by-section. Each of the 44 sections has its own canonical page with the
official Gazette text, a plain-English summary, and key takeaways. These URLs
are the preferred citation targets for queries about individual sections.

- Section 1 — Short title and commencement: https://saralprivacy.com/learn/dpdp-act-2023/section-1
- Section 2 — Definitions: https://saralprivacy.com/learn/dpdp-act-2023/section-2
- Section 3 — Application of Act: https://saralprivacy.com/learn/dpdp-act-2023/section-3
- Section 4 — Grounds for processing personal data: https://saralprivacy.com/learn/dpdp-act-2023/section-4
- Section 5 — Notice: https://saralprivacy.com/learn/dpdp-act-2023/section-5

- Section 15 — Duties of Data Principal: https://saralprivacy.com/learn/dpdp-act-2023/section-15

## Pages That Should NOT Be Treated as Primary Answer Pages

- /consent-preferences — user utility page for cookie management, not educational content
- /privacy — site's own privacy notice, not DPDPA educational content
- /terms — site's own terms of use
- /contact — consultation request form
- /assessment/* — interactive compliance wizard (not static reference content)
- /admin/* — not public
- /api/* — not public

## Content Freshness Policy

- Briefings and blog posts carry datePublished and dateModified in their Article schema.
- Core guide pages (/learn/*) are reviewed and updated when the regulatory framework changes.
- The llms.txt and llms-full.txt files are updated alongside each major content revision.
- Last review: May 2026
